extracted.intended_audience: writers and teachers of flash creative nonfiction (brevity), contributors to Brevity and similar journals
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for writing, teaching, and editing very short creative nonfiction (flash CNF), especially pieces intended for venues like Brevity that impose tight word limits. Emphasizes craft moves—title, compression, voice, image, form—and pedagogical approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Word-count constraint (Brevity: 750 words or fewer)
rubrics_metrics.description: Brevity holds writers to 750 words or fewer; the shortness is posed as a defining constraint and challenge of the form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The limit is 'daunting but appealing' and 'necessary'—it forces writers to compress material and rethink conventions. Writers may explicitly consider whether titles count; the constraint prompts strategic choices about what to include and how to economize language. Example/anti-pattern: some writers admit to 'cheating' by using long titles or hyphenated words to affect counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concision of language and single-image focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Flash nonfiction often shares with poetry a concision of language and the importance of a single image.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Think in metaphoric terms (a brief flash of lightning illuminating a figure) and let a striking image carry much of the piece’s weight. Prioritize precise, economical language that makes each word pull its weight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make the title 'work' (title as craft element)
rubrics_metrics.description: The title should do active thematic or formal work—like a poem's title—shedding light on and deepening the piece.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid merely prescriptive or neutral titles; choose metaphoric or layered titles that extend the essay’s meaning. Consider the title as part of the prose package (some writers deliberately use long or provocative titles to add content or play with word counts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Compression-driven turn/ending
rubrics_metrics.description: Compression in flash creates and sharpens the turn at the end of the essay—the moment where something 'rises that resonates.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pay close attention to how reduction and economizing shape the culminating shift or revelation. The limited space should intensify the turn rather than obscure it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimentation with voice(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Flash invites experimentation with voice, including voices that would not sustain a longer piece—communal/collective voices, personae, or sharply ironic detachment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use voice strategically: a persona, a communal tone, or a voice combining local sounds can create texture and tension. Flash can surface voices (even ones unsustainable in long form) that illuminate perspective and theme.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blurring genres and form boundaries
rubrics_metrics.description: Flash CNF often operates in the spaces between poetry/prose and fiction/nonfiction; resisting strict genre borders is common and permissible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don't feel compelled to fit tidy genre categories; use the form’s elasticity to mix narrative, lyric, metaphor, and factual elements. Critics or institutions may try to sort pieces, but the form benefits from genre-defying work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of image, metaphor, and lyric techniques
rubrics_metrics.description: The form accommodates and often benefits from concentrated use of image, metaphor, and lyric approaches as much as narrative moves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can tell a story, work with image and metaphor, or present a personal/nature essay—choose the sub-form that best serves the compressed moment and let lyric techniques carry associative weight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Texture of sounds and competing tones
rubrics_metrics.description: Creating a texture of sounds and placing competing tones or personas in tension can generate urgency and meaning in limited space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow different registers or community voices to converse or clash within the piece—this call-and-response can clarify sensibilities and create richness despite brevity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form as invitation to fragmentation and collage
rubrics_metrics.description: Segmented prose, collage, or fragmented structures are valid and useful strategies for flash; sections can function both as part of a whole and as stand-alone pieces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teach and employ collage/segmentation as a compositional method: brief sections can interplay to create cumulative effect, and the piece may be constructed from individual units that also resonate independently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creative reuse of conventions (titles, hyphenation) and anti-pattern awareness
rubrics_metrics.description: Writers may creatively exploit or subvert conventional expectations (long titles, hyphenated words) to manipulate perceived length or effect—but such tactics can be seen as 'cheating' or experimental.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of these tactics: they are a form of formal play (e.g., long titles adding 'word count' or hyphenation compressing words). Decide whether this play serves the piece artistically or merely circumvents the challenge of brevity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Versatility: suitability for many subforms
rubrics_metrics.description: Anything is possible within flash CNF: narrative story, image-driven lyric, personal essay, nature writing, or experimental fragments all fit the form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approach the form as an open table—choose the subform that best expresses the moment. Review anthologies (In Short, Sudden Fiction) to see examples across subgenres.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of irony and unusual perspectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Flash allows the writer to push irony and detachment and to present unusual angles that might not work in longer forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage irony or unusual narrative stances to reveal theme economically; these perspectives can 'show' rather than narrate extensive context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pedagogical directions for teaching flash
rubrics_metrics.description: When teaching the brief essay, offer concrete, compact directions such as: make the title work, teach collage/segmented prose, and instruct students to attend to compression and the end turn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different instructors favor different emphases—some teach collage instead of only compression; others stress the final turn. Offer exercises that isolate title-making, compression, voice, and segmentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formalist attention to conventions to defamiliarize and recontextualize
rubrics_metrics.description: A formalist approach—knowing forms inside out and then defamiliarizing them—helps writers recontextualize conventions for creative effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study existing forms and conventions, then use compression to defamiliarize expected moves (titles, narrative arcs, voice) so the piece feels fresh rather than derivative.
